ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.77 (excess distance fare) to the rider's original payment method; record a driver violation for an uninformed reroute (RD-2); send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log it on his route compliance record; and flag_account for the repeat deviation under RD-6.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 13.1 km against an 8.3 km optimal route, +4.8 km (+58%), over the 1 km tolerance in RD-1 [F1], and the code confirms the whole excess sits in one off-route segment 09:07–09:14 of 5.77 km where the optimal route covers 1.10 km [F3].

That segment is a deviation for which the driver proposed "mind if I go round via Marina Boulevard?" at 09:03 [F7]. The chat record is complete and timestamped and contains only that one message, with no rider reply [F8], and the rider's complaint says he did not reply. RD-5 requires a rider acknowledgment before or at the point of deviation; silence after a driver's question is not acknowledgment, and the road-name check is never reached, so the whole 4.67 km/4.80 km counts and no km is exempt [F7][F8][RD-5].

The driver's written statement that the rider gave "no objection" was made after the trip and is a claim, not the in-app chat or call recording RD-5 requires [F9][RD-5]. The rider's own silence in the complete chat record therefore settles consent against him [F8][RD-5].

A traffic reason exists on the replaced stretch — New Bridge Road at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 08:54–09:14, straddling the segment, with no recorded incident elsewhere [F10][F13][RD-4] — but a traffic reason only removes the driver-violation characterisation; it does not exempt the segment from refund, which under RD-2 turns on whether the rider was informed and agreed [RD-2]. Since he was not, RD-2's uninformed-traffic row applies: refund of the excess distance fare only, with a driver violation recorded [RD-2].

Amount: "(4.80 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4097/km = $6.77" [F4][RD-2]. This matches the billed excess distance of $6.77 [F4]; base, time fare, platform fee and tolls are not refunded [F6][RD-2]. No surge applies (1.0×) [F5].

RD-6 is met: the driver has 2 upheld route deviations in the last 90 days [F16], so flag_account is required on top of the refund [RD-6]; the rider's clean history [F15] does not decide anything. The amount is under $10, so a final system ruling is permitted [TH-1][TH-2].

segment_findings.reason: Driver proposed a reroute by chat at 09:03 [F7] but the complete, timestamped chat record [F8] shows no rider message before or at the 09:07 segment start; RD-5 needs a rider acknowledgment, and the driver's post-trip statement of 'no objection' is a claim only [F9] — so the segment is not exempt and counts in full.

rejected_claims.reason: Notice and consent are separate limbs of RD-5; the driver's 09:03 message [F7] gave notice but the complete chat record [F8] shows no rider acknowledgment, so the proposal alone does not make the segment exempt [RD-5].
The road-name check applies only once there is an agreement; with no rider acknowledgment in [F7]/[F8], MARINA BOULEVARD being among the roads driven [F3] is not reached [RD-5].

A no-objection case still fails the acknowledgment limb of RD-5 where the chat record [F8] shows no rider message, so the segment is not exempt under RD-3/RD-5; the only reduction available is that the fare refund stays at the excess distance fare [F4][RD-2].
RD-7's reminder is a first-incident remedy only; the driver's record shows 2 upheld route deviations in 90 days [F16], meeting the RD-6 repeat condition, so flag_account applies as well [RD-6].

No driver violation is recorded for the traffic question: New Bridge Road was at band 2 during 08:54–09:14 [F10], satisfying RD-4 [RD-4]. The account flag instead rests on the repeat-deviation condition in [F16][RD-6].
